about.title: Personal Injury Help in Mill Valley, California
about.longDescription: Mill Valley may feel like a quiet corner of Marin County, but its roads still see their share of collisions. Public records show 43 injury crashes in the most recent year, leaving 60 people hurt. Miller Avenue, Camino Alto, E Blithedale Avenue, and the US-101 corridor account for a large share of these reported incidents, and Friday midday hours tend to see more activity than other times of the week. Whether you were driving through downtown, walking near the plaza, or merging onto the freeway, an unexpected collision can upend your routine fast — medical visits, missed work, and calls from insurance adjusters all at once. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We don't handle your case ourselves; instead, we connect injured people in Mill Valley with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details and explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no cost and no obligation to see what your situation might involve — just a straightforward first step toward getting the right information.

whyChoose.title: What Mill Valley Residents Should Know About California Injury Law

items.title: A Filing Clock That Doesn't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long to explore your options can close doors you didn't know were closing.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in typical injury cases. That matters when an injury affects your daily life well beyond medical bills.

items.title: You Don't Pay Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money. That structure lets injured people get legal help without worrying about hourly fees.

items.question: How much time do I have to file a claim after a crash in Mill Valley?
items.answer: In most California injury cases, you have two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If a government vehicle or entity was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to check sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the collision?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you share some blame. Your recovery amount is adjusted based on your percentage of fault, not denied outright.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Mill Valley?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along Miller Avenue, Camino Alto, E Blithedale Avenue, and the US-101 corridor, with Friday midday hours seeing more reported activity. These are simply the roads and times with the most recorded incidents, not a judgment about any location.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in standard personal injury cases. This differs from some other states and can matter significantly for long-term recovery.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you actually recover compensation.
